propositions: A store write whose lock acquisition times out within the budget is permanently discarded with no retry or spool, causing data loss.

The current acquire() implementation computes a single deadline from timeout * attempts, where attempts acts as a silent multiplier rather than enabling a retry loop, and both fcntl and mkdir legs poll non-blocking with jitter, yielding no fairness.

Holder duration (not writer count) now drives write loss: a 70-second holder causes all subsequent writes to lose within the 60-second budget; a 45-second holder causes claim writes to fail at exactly 30.30 seconds.

Bounded retry-with-backoff inside acquire() is the correct remedy because fair queueing cannot help when a single holder exceeds the entire budget; retrying an acquisition cannot replay the write body because the retry loop is strictly inside acquire() and exits before the caller runs.

The design opts in exactly five call sites (3 in event_append.py, 1 in txn.py, 1 in push.py) to read REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES and retry with exponential backoff (0.5s, 1.0s capped at 2.0s), raising LockTimeout with cumulative wait only after all passes exhaust; all other callers keep fail-fast via retries=0 default.

The retry ceiling is ~181.5 seconds (3 passes × 60s + ~1.5s backoff), converting write loss into latency for holders within this bound, while preserving fail-fast for advisory/best-effort operations and repair utilities.
